prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” personal injury lawyer for every car-accident claim — the right attorney depends on the facts of your case, the lawyer’s experience with cases like yours, and how well you work together. That said, Chicago has many highly regarded personal injury firms; two long-established names are Clifford Law Offices and Salvi, Schostok & Pritchard, both known for major car‑crash and catastrophic‑injury work. (If you’d like, I can pull together a longer local shortlist based on ratings and specialties.)

How to choose the best attorney for your case
- Relevant experience: Look for attorneys who handle car-accident/personal-injury claims frequently and who have experience with cases that match your injury severity, liability issues, or insurance disputes.
- Trial and verdict experience: Many cases settle, but you want a lawyer who will try the case if necessary.
- Track record: Ask about past settlements/verdicts and outcomes for similar cases.
- Reputation and references: Check peer ratings (Super Lawyers, Martindale‑Hubbell), client reviews, and ask the lawyer for references.
- Resources: Complex cases need a firm with investigators, accident reconstructionists, medical experts, and the ability to cover upfront costs.
- Communication style: Confirm how often you’ll get updates and who handles day‑to‑day communications.
- Fee structure: Most PI lawyers work on contingency (no fee unless you recover). Get the exact percentage and how costs (medical records, experts, filing fees) are handled if you don’t recover.
- Local courtroom knowledge: Familiarity with Cook County judges and local procedures is useful.

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- How many car-accident cases have you handled? How many went to trial?
- Have you handled cases like mine (type/severity of injury, disputed fault, uninsured/underinsured motorist)?
- What’s a realistic settlement range for my case and why?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day?
- What is your contingency fee and how are expenses handled?
- Can you provide recent case results and client references?

Practical next steps right now
- Seek/continue medical care and preserve medical records.
- Preserve evidence: photos, dashcam, witness contact info, police report number.
- Don’t give recorded statements to the insurer or sign releases without an attorney.
- Be mindful of Illinois deadlines: in many injury cases the statute of limitations is 2 years (confirm with an attorney promptly).

If you want, I can:
- Recommend several Chicago attorneys/firms (I’ll base selections on prominence, reputation, and specialties) — tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood.
- Draft an email you can send to lawyers asking the right questions before a consultation.
- Help you prepare for a consultation and list what documents to bring.

Which would you prefer?
